prompt:
Create ONE transparent-background, orthographic pixel-art six-view atlas for the small bugbear timber shelter shown in the attached reference sheet. Match the Pocket Dungeon palette, pixel clusters, dark outline and gold-brown log materials. The source icon is a hybrid/isometric map symbol; use it only for identity. Use the accepted TOP and BOTTOM examples for plan shape and material guidance. Do not copy the source's angled camera.

Exactly 6 columns in this order: FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. One row, six equal isolated cells. Each cell contains the same whole physical shelter, centered, no labels, no shadows, no cell bleed. Strict axis-aligned orthographic views, camera exactly along world axes, no perspective, no isometric angle, no foreshortening, no diagonal corner view. Keep object world orientation fixed across all six views. FRONT is viewed from -Y, REAR from +Y, RIGHT from +X, LEFT from -X, TOP straight down +Z, BOTTOM straight up from -Z.

The shelter is an upright compact timber/log hut with a red hide canopy roof, four spiked log corner posts, an open dark front entrance and two small wooden barrels at the front. FRONT is a straight-on broad facade; show the entrance centered between the two posts and the same canopy as a shallow roof edge above. REAR is the opposite straight-on broad timber back wall under the roof; no doorway visible from rear. RIGHT and LEFT are straight side elevations: each is a single side wall plane, with the same four-corner-post height and roof edge; do not show the front and side walls together. Keep the vertical post height equal in all four elevations. TOP is the canopy's rectangular plan with the red hide and cross-braces as shown by the accepted TOP example. BOTTOM is the compact ground footprint with post foot ends and closed underside as shown by the accepted BOTTOM example. No invented rooms, extra barrels, windows, props, or people. Transparent background, crisp pixel-art clusters.
